questions.stem: Which is the negation of “every vertex has at least one edge”?
options: Some vertex has at least one edge
Exactly one vertex has no edge
questions.explain: To negate “every”, one counterexample is enough: some vertex has no edge.

questions.stem: The neighbour sets of two vertices are N(u) = {2, 3, 5} and N(v) = {3, 4, 5}. How many common neighbours do they have?
questions.explain: Common neighbours form the intersection {3, 5}, which has 2 elements.

questions.stem: The relation R = {(1,2), (2,1), (2,3), (3,2)} on {1, 2, 3} has which property?
questions.explain: Every pair has its reverse in R, so R is symmetric. It is not reflexive, not transitive ((1,2) and (2,3) need (1,3)) and not antisymmetric.

questions.stem: Two numbers in {0, 1, …, 8} are related when they leave the same remainder on division by 3. This is an equivalence relation. How many equivalence classes does it have?
questions.explain: There is one class for each possible remainder 0, 1 and 2, so 3 classes of 3 numbers each.
